::: {.hero}
# Jakob Kasper

[PhD researcher in political psychology, University of Amsterdam]{.lede}
:::

<img src="jakob.jpg" class="headshot" alt="Portrait of Jakob Kasper"/>

I am a **PhD candidate** at the [University of Amsterdam](https://www.uva.nl/profiel/k/a/j.kasper/j.kasper.html) (Amsterdam School of Communication Research). My PhD is part of the MSCA doctoral network [Interdisciplinary Perspectives on the Politics of Adolescence and Democracy](https://www.ippad.eu/) (IP-PAD), and I am affiliated with the [Hot Politics Lab](https://www.hotpolitics.eu/) and the [Center for Politics and Communication](https://www.polcomm.org/about-2/).

My research focuses mainly on **affective polarization**. I explore how it can be measured within **multiparty systems**, and I aim to connect political science's understanding of affective polarization with psychological **theories of affect**, refining both theoretical frameworks and measurement tools to better capture its affective nature. I also investigate how affective polarization develops during **adolescence**, seeking to understand its origins and to address concerns about increasing polarization among younger generations. Moreover, I am interested in the implications of (affective) polarization for **political behavior and democratic attitudes**, as well as efforts to reduce it. 

Before my PhD, I earned a Bachelor's and Master's degree in Psychology at the University of Heidelberg (Germany) and spent a year as a graduate exchange student at Cornell University (USA).
